summary.en: Eggs cooked into tomatoes and green pepper. They are never beaten and rarely stirred, or you end up with ordinary scrambled eggs.

text.en: Slice the peppers into rings and fry them in the two fats for three or four minutes, until the edges start to darken.
Add the tomatoes, salt them and cook over medium heat for ten minutes. Wait for the oil to separate and glisten at the edges — that is the sign the water has gone.
Lower the heat, break the eggs straight into the sauce and scatter the pepper flakes. Stir slowly and only two or three times, leaving streaks of yolk.
Take it off when the white has set and the yolk is still loose: the pan finishes the job. Scatter over the oregano and the cheese.

summary.en: A red lentil soup blended smooth and finished with lemon and paprika butter.

text.en: Fry the onion and carrot in a spoon of butter until soft, add the tomato paste and give it another minute, until it darkens.
Add the lentils, potato and water, bring to the boil and simmer for twenty-five minutes, until the lentils have collapsed completely.
Blend until entirely smooth. The soup should be thick but still pourable; loosen it with boiling water if it is not.
Melt the rest of the butter, take it off the heat and stir in the mint and paprika. Ladle out the soup, spoon the butter over and serve with a wedge of lemon.

summary.en: Slices of döner over pieces of pide, under tomato sauce, melted butter and yoghurt.

text.en: Slice the lamb very thin, season it and leave it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil, add the pepper paste and warm it a minute.
Add the passata and oregano and cook the sauce fifteen minutes to thicken it.
Cut the pide into cubes and dry them in the oven at 180 °C for eight minutes.
Sear the lamb slices over a very high flame in batches, a minute and a half each.
Spread the bread on the plates, spoon over some of the sauce, then the meat and the rest of the sauce.
Melt the butter until it sizzles and pour it over the meat. Put the yoghurt at the side and serve with fried peppers.

summary.en: A paper-thin flatbread with lamb and pepper paste, baked three minutes in a screaming oven.

text.en: Knead a dough from the flour, water, yeast and salt for eight minutes and prove it an hour.
Blend the onion, pepper and tomato and press the purée through a sieve: the spare water is not wanted.
Mix the lamb with the vegetable purée, the pepper paste, chopped parsley, flakes and salt. It should be as thick as a pâté.
Heat the oven with a stone at full power for forty minutes.
Roll the balls of dough paper-thin, twenty-five centimetres across, and spread the topping thinly right to the edges.
Bake on the stone three or four minutes. The edges should colour and the middle stay soft: a lahmacun is rolled up to eat.

summary.en: Pork on skewers in lemon, oregano and olive oil, cooked fast over a fierce heat.

text.en: Mix the oil, lemon juice and zest, oregano, crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Coat the meat and leave it two hours, and no more than four.
While it marinates, make the tzatziki: yoghurt with the squeezed cucumber, a clove of garlic, a spoon of oil and salt.
Thread the meat onto skewers loosely — the heat has to get between the pieces. A tightly packed skewer stays raw in the middle.
Cook on a hot grill or griddle, three minutes on each of the four sides. The meat should darken rather than pale.
Rest the meat for five minutes, warm the pitas thirty seconds a side, and serve with the tzatziki and lemon.

summary.en: Flat beef patties with cornmeal, tomato and whole coriander seeds.

text.en: Mix the mince with the cornmeal, egg, onion, chilli, coriander leaf, crushed coriander seed, pomegranate seeds and salt.
Fold in the tomatoes last so they do not weep too early, and chill the mixture for twenty minutes.
With wet hands shape flat patties twelve centimetres across and a centimetre thick.
Heat half a centimetre of ghee and fry them three or four minutes a side over medium heat, uncovered.
Serve with flatbread, onion rings and lemon. Traditionally an egg is broken over each patty in the pan.

summary.en: A lentil stew finished by pouring sizzling spiced fat over it. That step is the dish.

text.en: Cover the lentils with three cups of water, add the turmeric and simmer covered for thirty minutes, until the grains collapse into a soft mass.
Mash some of the lentils against the side of the pot and season. The consistency should be that of a thick soup.
Separately fry the onion until golden, add the tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce. Stir that into the lentils.
Heat the ghee in a small pan until it is just short of smoking. Add the mustard seeds; they should crackle within seconds.
Add the cumin at once, the garlic and chillies ten seconds later, the asafoetida twenty seconds after that. The whole thing takes under a minute and cannot be left alone.
Pour the sizzling tadka straight into the lentils — it should hiss. Stir once and serve with rice or flatbread.

summary.en: Spinach blanched and blended, with cubes of paneer. Spinach must not be stewed or it goes brown.

text.en: Drop the spinach into boiling water for ninety seconds and move it straight into iced water. Squeeze it out and blend it with the chilli to a purée.
Soak the paneer in hot salted water for ten minutes, then drain it.
Fry the cumin seeds in the ghee until they crackle, add the onion and cook it gold, then the ginger and garlic for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they break down and the fat starts separating at the edges.
Stir in the spinach purée, garam masala and salt, and warm it for exactly a minute. Add the paneer and cream and take it off the heat.

summary.en: Tiny lamb dumplings, boiled and served under garlic yoghurt and paprika butter.

text.en: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover it and rest it forty minutes, or the dough springs back as you roll it.
Mix the mince with the grated onion, salt and pepper and squeeze out the excess juice.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut it into two-centimetre squares.
Put a knife-tip of filling on each square and pinch the four corners up into a knot.
Boil the mantı in salted water for eight minutes and drain, keeping a ladle of the water.
Whisk the yoghurt with the garlic, plate the mantı, spoon the yoghurt over and pour on the paprika and mint butter.

summary.en: A fiery tomato stew with merguez lamb sausages and eggs stirred into the sauce.

text.en: Fry the merguez in olive oil until browned all over and lift them onto a plate.
In the same fat fry the sliced pepper and the garlic until soft.
Stir in the harissa, tomato paste and caraway and cook them two minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season and cook fifteen minutes to thicken.
Return the sausages, cut into pieces, and warm them three minutes.
Drop the heat to its lowest, break in the eggs and stir with a spatula for three minutes into a creamy mass.
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with baguette.

summary.en: Beef cut into strips and seared hard, in a soured cream sauce with onion.

text.en: Cut the beef across the grain into centimetre strips, pat them dry and pepper them.
Heat a pan hard and sear the beef in batches for ninety seconds, without turning it often.
Lift out the meat and fry the mushrooms over a high flame until their water has gone.
Add the butter and onion and fry until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour, cook it a minute and add the stock, stirring until smooth.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the soured cream and mustard, and season.
Return the meat with its juices, warm it a minute without boiling and scatter with parsley.

summary.en: Tomatoes cooked down in olive oil with chilli and garlic to a thick sauce.

text.en: Cut the tomatoes into large wedges, skins and seeds left in.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the onion in it.
Add the crushed garlic and the whole green chillies and warm them a minute.
Tip in the tomatoes, salt them and stew over a medium heat, stirring now and then.
Crush the tomatoes with a spoon once the skins start to lift from the flesh.
Reduce it fifteen minutes more, until the oil rises at the edges as a separate layer.
Scatter with dried mint and serve it in the pan with flatbread.

summary.en: Potato pancakes from raw grated potato, fried to a crisp edge and served with soured cream.

text.en: Grate the potato and onion finely into the same bowl.
Let the mass stand three minutes and pour off the water that gathers on top, leaving the sediment.
Season with salt and pepper. Add nothing else.
Heat the oil over medium and drop the mixture in by the spoonful, flattening it to half a centimetre.
Fry three to four minutes a side, to a deep golden crisp crust.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with soured cream and dill.

summary.en: Godamba roti chopped on the griddle with vegetables, egg and curry, worked with two cleavers.

text.en: Cut the roti into centimetre strips: that makes the chopping easier later.
Heat a large pan with the oil, fry the onion, leek and chilli two minutes, add the carrot and cabbage and cook three more.
Push the vegetables aside, break the eggs into the cleared space, let them set and break them up.
Add the chicken, curry powder and strips of roti and start chopping with two spatulas, mixing as you go. Three minutes of real work.
Pour the curry sauce down the side and keep chopping a minute more. The mixture should be moist but not wet.

summary.en: A saffron risotto built on stock and near-constant stirring, which is what pulls the starch out of the rice and makes it creamy.

text.en: Steep the saffron in a ladle of hot stock and set it aside. Keep the rest of the stock at a bare simmer — cold stock stops the cooking.
Melt half the butter and sweat the onion over low heat until soft and translucent without letting it colour, about eight minutes.
Add the rice and stir for a couple of minutes until the grains are translucent at the edges and milky in the centre. This is the tostatura, and it keeps the grains intact.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely — the smell of alcohol has to go.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, waiting until the rice has nearly absorbed it before the next. Around eighteen minutes, until the grain is soft outside with a slight bite in the middle.
Stir in the saffron infusion, take the pan off the heat and beat in the cold butter and parmesan, shaking the pan hard. The risotto should spread slowly across the plate.

summary.en: Skinless minced-meat sausages over coals, with raw onion and somun flatbread.

text.en: Combine all three minces with the crushed garlic, bicarbonate, paprika, salt and pepper.
Work it by hand for ten minutes, adding the iced water a little at a time, until the mass turns tacky and even.
Press film onto the surface and refrigerate for at least twelve hours.
With wet hands roll sausages eight centimetres long and as thick as a thumb.
Grill over hot coals or on a griddle three minutes a side, turning once.
Split the warm somun, tuck the ćevapi inside and add a pile of raw onion and kajmak.

summary.en: Mussels steamed in white wine with celery and onion. Five minutes under a lid, no longer.

text.en: Sort the mussels: discard any that are cracked or that will not close when tapped. Pull away the beards and rinse them under the tap.
Melt the butter in a wide pot and sweat the shallot, celery and garlic for five minutes without letting them colour.
Pour in the wine, add the thyme and bay and bring it to the boil.
Tip in the mussels, cover at once and hold them over a fierce flame for five minutes, shaking the pot a couple of times.
Lift the lid: the shells should be open. Throw out any that are not. Scatter parsley, add pepper and serve with chips and the broth in a separate cup.

summary.en: Fried rice with a chilli and shrimp-paste base, sweet soy sauce and an egg on top.

text.en: Pound the shallot, garlic, chilli and terasi to a paste in a mortar. It smells aggressive; that is correct, frying softens it.
Heat the wok and fry the paste in the oil for two minutes, until it darkens and the smell turns deep.
Add the chicken and fry three minutes, then the prawns and cabbage for two more.
Tip in the cold rice, breaking up the lumps with the spatula, pour in the kecap manis and fry over a high flame for three minutes, tossing constantly.
Fry the eggs separately until the edges are lacy and the yolks loose. Serve the rice with an egg on top, slices of cucumber and fried shallots.

summary.en: Trout baked whole with lemon and herbs, from Lake Ohrid.

text.en: Rinse the trout, pat them dry and cut two slashes on each side.
Rub the fish with salt, pepper, paprika and olive oil inside and out.
Tuck lemon slices, garlic, parsley and thyme into each cavity.
Slice the potatoes thin and lay them overlapping on an oiled tray.
Set the fish on the potatoes and pour over the wine and the remaining oil.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, until the skin colours.
Test at the spine and serve straight from the tray with a wedge of lemon.

summary.en: A cold yoghurt soup with cucumber, garlic, dill and walnuts.

text.en: Grate the cucumbers coarsely or dice them small and salt them.
Leave the cucumber ten minutes to give up its water, but do not pour that water away.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste so it does not turn up in pieces.
Grind the walnuts to a fine crumb, keeping a few larger pieces back.
Whisk the yoghurt with the cold water until even and add the garlic and walnuts.
Stir in the cucumber with its juice, the chopped dill and the sunflower oil.
Chill it an hour and serve with an ice cube in each bowl.

summary.en: Raw kibbeh: the freshest lamb pounded with bulgur and spices, served under olive oil.

name.en: Mint and white onion to serve
name.tr: Mint and white onion to serve

text.en: Soak the bulgur in cold water for ten minutes, drain and squeeze it dry. Chill the bowl — everything for nayyeh must stay cold.
Trim the lamb of fat and silverskin down to clean muscle and cube it. Blitz with the onion to a smooth paste without letting the bowl warm up.
Add the bulgur, spices, mint and salt. Knead, wetting your hands with iced water, until the paste is smooth and glossy.
Spread the paste over a cold plate about a centimetre and a half thick, press grooves with the back of a spoon and pour the olive oil over generously.
Serve at once, with mint leaves, white onion wedges and flatbread. Nayyeh is not kept: leftovers are fried as patties the same evening.

summary.en: Flaky fatir bread soaked in reconstituted dried qurut, under fried onion and fresh vegetables.

text.en: Cover the qurut with hot water for twenty minutes and rub it by hand into an even liquid.
Pass it through a sieve to remove any grains. The liquid should be like thin soured cream.
Slice the onion into rings and fry it in oil until golden, ten minutes.
Tear the fatir into large pieces into a wide dish.
Pour the qurut over the bread and leave it five minutes to soak.
Top with the fried onion and its oil, then the tomato, cucumber and herbs.

summary.en: Potato dumplings with sheep's brynza and bacon crackling. Slovakia's national dish.

text.en: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly; only a little water should go, as a dry mass will not bind.
Mix in the flour, egg and salt. The mass should slide off a spoon slowly rather than pour.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp and lift it out, keeping the fat.
Push the dough into boiling salted water through a colander with large holes. The dumplings are done when they float, after about three minutes.
Drain the dumplings, return them to the warm pan and stir in the brynza with a spoon of the cooking water. Keep the heat off.
Serve into bowls, spoon over the hot fat and scatter the crackling on top.

summary.en: A cold tomato soup blended with bread and oil into an emulsion — that is what makes it thick rather than watery.

text.en: Soak the bread crumb in cold water for ten minutes and squeeze it dry.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, garlic and bread until completely smooth. It takes longer than you expect — a good two minutes at full speed.
With the blender still running, pour the oil in a thin stream. The soup pales and thickens: that is the emulsion.
Add the vinegar and salt, taste and season again. Pass it through a sieve for a silkier texture and chill for at least two hours.

summary.en: Cubes of beef seared over high heat, on salad, with a dip of lime and black pepper.

text.en: Marinate the beef in the oyster and soy sauces with garlic, sugar and half the pepper for twenty minutes.
Mix the lime juice with the remaining pepper and a pinch of salt; that is the dipping sauce.
Arrange the lettuce, tomato and cucumber slices and red onion rings on a platter.
Heat a pan as high as it goes and sear the beef in batches, a minute and a half each, without stirring constantly.
Fry the eggs, keeping the yolks runny.
Pile the beef on the vegetables, top with the eggs and give everyone their own small bowl of the dip.

summary.en: Raw fish in lime juice with onion and ají. It marinates for minutes, not hours — longer and it is cooked through.

text.en: Soak the sliced onion in iced water for ten minutes and pat it dry: the harshness goes, the flavour stays.
Squeeze the limes by hand rather than in a press: pressure on the skin releases bitter oils.
Salt the fish, mix it with the chopped ají and coriander, pour the lime over and leave it exactly three to five minutes. The edges turn opaque and the middle stays translucent.
Add the onion, toss once and serve at once with the sweet potato and corn. Pour the juice from the bowl into small glasses.

summary.en: Green chillies stewed in cheese. Bhutan's national dish, where chilli is a vegetable rather than a seasoning.

text.en: Quarter the chillies lengthways. The seeds stay in; in Bhutan they are not removed.
Put the chillies, sliced onion, garlic and tomato in a pan and add water to the same level.
Bring it up and cook ten minutes, until the chillies soften.
Crumble the cheese in, drop the heat and leave it two minutes; it should begin melting on its own.
Stir it into a creamy sauce, add the butter and salt cautiously; the cheese is salty.
Serve with the red rice Bhutanese cook to a slightly sticky texture.

summary.en: Danish meat patties — flat rather than round — fried in butter to a dark crust.

text.en: Mix both minces with the grated onion, egg, flour, salt, pepper and allspice.
Work it for five minutes, adding the milk in stages. The mixture should turn tacky and string off the spoon.
Chill it for half an hour: cold farce holds its shape better.
Melt the butter over medium heat. With a spoon dipped in water, scoop the mixture into the pan and flatten each one.
Fry six minutes a side, to a dark brown crust. Do not hurry: the colour is the flavour.
Serve with boiled potatoes, pickled red cabbage and the gravy from the pan.

summary.en: Diced chicken with peanuts and dried chillies in a sauce where the vinegar matters more than the sugar.

text.en: Mix the chicken with the egg white, a spoon of cornflour, a spoon of soy and a pinch of salt, and leave it twenty minutes.
Mix the sauce in advance: vinegar, the rest of the soy, the sugar and the rest of the cornflour with two spoons of water. Keep it within reach — there is no time to mix it later.
Heat the oil and fry the chillies with the Sichuan pepper for twenty seconds, until dark but not black. Burnt chilli turns bitter.
Add the chicken and leave it alone for a minute, then toss and cook through — two minutes more.
Throw in the garlic, ginger and the white of the spring onion, then after half a minute pour in the sauce. It thickens in seconds. Off the heat, add the peanuts and the green of the onion.

summary.en: A whole fish steamed with ginger and spring onion, finished with smoking oil and soy.

text.en: Dry the fish, cut two slashes on each side and rub it with salt and wine.
Lay a few spring onion stalks on a plate and set the fish on them, so steam reaches it from below too.
Tuck half the ginger into the slashes and the cavity.
Set the plate into a boiling steamer and cook eight minutes for every centimetre of thickness.
Pour off all the liquid from the plate and discard it; it is bitter.
Scatter the remaining ginger, shredded spring onion and coriander over the top.
Heat the oil until it smokes and pour it over the aromatics, then pour the soy and sugar around the edge of the plate.

summary.en: The village salad, with no leaves in it: tomato, cucumber, onion, olives and a whole slab of feta on top.

text.en: Cut the tomatoes into large wedges and salt them straight in the bowl. Leave them five minutes: the juice they give up becomes the base of the dressing.
Add the cucumber, pepper and onion. Mix with your hands rather than a spoon — nothing breaks that way.
Scatter the olives over, lay the slab of feta on top and pour the oil over everything at once. Sprinkle the oregano straight onto the feta, where the oil will open it up.

summary.en: Chicken in a saffron marinade with onion juice and lemon, grilled over coals.

text.en: Grind the saffron with a pinch of sugar and steep it in three spoons of warm water for fifteen minutes.
Grate the onions finely and squeeze the juice through muslin, discarding the pulp.
Mix the onion juice, half the saffron infusion, the juice of two lemons, the yoghurt, oil, salt and pepper.
Cut the chicken into four-centimetre pieces, coat it in the marinade and refrigerate it eight hours.
Thread the pieces onto flat skewers packed tight and get the coals to an even strong heat.
Grill eight minutes a side, turning the skewer every two minutes.
Mix the melted butter with the remaining saffron and brush the kebabs before serving. Serve with rice, tomatoes and sumac.

summary.en: Whole sardines salted coarsely and grilled over coals, served on a slice of bread.

text.en: Rinse the sardines without gutting them and pat them dry on the outside.
Bury the fish in coarse salt on all sides and leave it half an hour at room temperature.
Light the coals and let them ash over; an open flame burns the skin within a minute.
Char the peppers on the coals, peel them and dress them with oil, garlic and vinegar.
Shake the excess salt off the fish and lay them on a hot, oiled grate.
Grill four minutes a side, turning them exactly once.
Lay the sardines on slices of bread and serve with boiled potatoes and the pepper salad.

summary.en: A sandwich of thin steak, ham, bacon, cheese and a fried egg. Uruguay's national dish.

text.en: Pound the beef under film to four millimetres and season it.
Fry the bacon crisp and drain it on paper.
Get the pan very hot and sear the steaks forty-five seconds a side.
Lay the cheese on the meat in the pan and cover it for thirty seconds so it softens.
Fry the eggs with runny yolks and toast the cut buns in a dry pan.
Spread mayonnaise on both halves and layer lettuce, tomato, the steak with its cheese, ham, bacon and the egg.
Close it, spear it with a cocktail stick and an olive, and serve with chips.

summary.en: A salad of vegetables and herbs with fried pieces of flatbread and sumac.

text.en: Tear the bread by hand into two-finger pieces and fry them in olive oil until browned.
Drain the bread on paper and dust it with half the sumac while it is still hot.
Cut the tomatoes, cucumbers and radishes into large uneven pieces; the salad should be rough rather than neat.
Tear the lettuce by hand and chop the herbs and spring onion.
Whisk a dressing from the lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, crushed garlic, the remaining sumac, oil and salt.
Toss the vegetables in the dressing, add the bread and serve at once.

summary.en: Tofu in a hot doubanjiang sauce with Sichuan pepper, which numbs rather than burns.

text.en: Slip the tofu into barely simmering salted water for three minutes and drain it gently.
Fry the pork until browned and its fat has rendered, then push it aside. Add the doubanjiang and fry for a minute, until the oil turns red.
Add the garlic, ginger and black beans, warm for half a minute and pour in the stock. Bring it to the boil.
Slide the tofu in and simmer for three minutes without stirring — swirl the pan instead, or the cubes break up.
Slake the cornflour in cold water and add it in two goes, letting the sauce come back to the boil each time. Off the heat, scatter over the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onion.

summary.en: A filo pie of spinach and feta. The spinach is squeezed bone dry, or the base stays raw.

text.en: Chop the spinach, salt it and leave it twenty minutes. Squeeze it dry by the handful — more water comes out than seems possible.
Fry the spring onion in a spoon of oil until soft and let it cool.
Mix the spinach with the onion, feta, dill, eggs, nutmeg and pepper. Taste before salting: the feta is salty already.
Line the tin with seven sheets of filo, brushing each with olive oil and letting the edges overhang.
Spread the filling, fold the overhanging edges in and cover with six more sheets, brushing each one.
Score the top into portions without cutting through to the filling, flick water over it and bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes, to a deep gold.

summary.en: A parsley salad with a little bulgur in it, not the other way round. There is ten times more herb than grain.

text.en: Rinse the bulgur and pour the juice of one lemon over it. Leave it to swell for fifteen minutes.
Wash the parsley well in advance and dry it thoroughly — an hour on a cloth is not too much. Strip the thick stems and chop it fine but without pulverising it.
Dice the tomatoes small and salt them separately: the juice they give up goes into the bulgur.
Mix everything with the juice of the second lemon, the oil and the allspice. Let it stand ten minutes before serving.

summary.en: A thick omelette of potato and onion, where the potato is not fried but poached in oil until it is nearly a purée.

ingredients.note: nearly all of it goes back in the bottle

text.en: Heat the oil in a deep pan until it is warm rather than hot — a slice of potato dropped in should sigh, not crackle. Add the potato and onion and salt them.
Poach for twenty minutes, turning gently now and then. It is ready when a slice breaks easily against the side of the pan. Drain through a colander, keeping the potato.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and fold the warm potato through them. Let it sit for ten minutes: the potato gives up starch and the tortilla holds together for it.
In a 24 cm pan with a spoon of oil, pour the mixture in and cook over medium heat for four minutes, easing the edges towards the middle with a spatula.
Cover with a plate, flip in one movement and slide it back raw side down. Three minutes more leaves the centre slightly loose, which is how it should be.

summary.en: Wide rice noodles seared over a very high flame with prawns, egg and bean sprouts.

text.en: Separate the fresh noodles into individual strips by hand, trying not to tear them.
Set everything out beside the hob — the cooking takes four minutes and there will be no time to fetch anything.
Heat the wok until it smokes, melt the lard and fry the garlic and sausage for twenty seconds.
Add the prawns and cockles and cook thirty seconds, without stirring constantly.
Push everything to the side, break the eggs into the centre, let them set for ten seconds and break them up.
Add the noodles, both soy sauces, the sambal and sugar and toss them for a minute and a half.
Throw in the sprouts and chives, toss for twenty seconds and serve immediately.

summary.en: Cypriot cheese seared to a crust, with cold watermelon and mint. The island's summer plate.

text.en: Soak the halloumi in cold water for fifteen minutes, drain it and pat it completely dry.
Cut the cheese into centimetre slices — thinner and it dries out, thicker and it will not heat through.
Cut the chilled watermelon into large cubes and keep it in the fridge until serving.
Heat a dry pan hard and sear the halloumi two minutes a side, to dark stripes.
Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice, honey and pepper.
Arrange the watermelon, rocket and hot cheese, spoon over the dressing and scatter with mint. Serve at once.

summary.en: Beef seared in a wok with onion and tomato, served with both chips and rice at once.

text.en: Marinate the beef in the soy, vinegar and garlic for fifteen minutes, then pat it dry: a wet surface will not scorch.
Heat the pan until it smokes and sear the beef in two batches, ninety seconds each, leaving it alone for the first forty seconds. Set it aside.
In the same pan fry the onion and ají for ninety seconds — the onion should stay crisp inside.
Return the beef, pour in what is left of the marinade, add the tomatoes and warm through for half a minute. Take it off and stir in the coriander.
Serve with hot chips — some tossed into the pan so they take up the sauce — and a separate helping of rice.

summary.en: Salt cod with matchstick potatoes and egg that binds everything without becoming an omelette.

text.en: Poach the soaked cod for five minutes, cool it and pull it into flakes by hand, discarding skin and bones. By hand rather than with a fork: that is how small bones are found.
Deep-fry the potato matchsticks at 180 °C to a crisp gold, in batches. Drain on a rack and salt them.
In a wide pan sweat the onion in the olive oil for ten minutes until soft and sweet, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the cod and warm it through for three minutes, then tip in the potato and toss.
Take the pan off the heat, pour in the beaten eggs and stir without stopping for half a minute, until they turn creamy. Scatter over the parsley and olives.

summary.en: A pie of thin pastry layered with spinach and brined cheese, each layer soaked in oil.

text.en: Scald the spinach with boiling water, drain it and wring it out dry by hand.
Chop the spinach and mix it with the crumbled cheese, spring onion, dill and pepper. Salt cautiously; the cheese is salty.
Oil a tin and lay in three sheets of filo, brushing each one.
Spread a third of the filling, cover with two oiled sheets and repeat twice more.
Finish with three sheets on top, tuck the edges in and brush generously with oil.
Score it into squares down to the base with a sharp knife; cutting it after baking will not work.
Bake at 190 °C for forty-five minutes, to a deep golden crisp crust.

summary.en: Chicken stewed without water in its own juices with tomatoes and a mountain of fresh herbs.

text.en: Brown the chicken pieces in a dry heavy pot without fat, to a golden crust.
Lift out the meat, add the butter and soften the onion in the rendered fat.
Skin the tomatoes, grate them and add them to the onion.
Return the chicken, season, add the khmeli suneli and the whole chilli and cover the pot.
Stew thirty minutes on a low heat, never adding water.
Chop all the herbs and the garlic coarsely, not to a paste.
Stir in the herbs and garlic, cover the pot, take it off the heat and let it stand ten minutes.

summary.en: An Albanian bake of peppers, tomatoes and curd cheese, served in its clay pan.

text.en: Char the peppers over a flame or under a grill until the skins blacken.
Put the hot peppers in a bag for ten minutes and peel them.
Soften the onion and garlic in butter and stir in a spoon of flour.
Add the chopped tomatoes and reduce them to a thick base with no loose liquid.
Cut the peeled peppers into strips and stir them into the tomato base.
Mash the curd cheese with the feta and work it into the hot mixture.
Transfer it to a clay pan and bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes, until it bubbles.

summary.en: A pie of crumpled filo sheets in a cheese and egg custard, baked to browned ridges.

text.en: Mash both cheeses with a fork and mix them with the eggs, kefir, soured cream and half the oil.
Stir in the sparkling water; it lightens the custard and keeps it from setting dense.
Taste the custard for salt: brined cheese varies, and it has to be adjusted rather than measured.
Oil the tin and lay two whole filo sheets flat on the bottom, uncrumpled.
Dip each remaining sheet in the custard, crumple it like a concertina and lay it in the tin.
Pour the remaining custard over, cover with two whole sheets and brush them with oil.
Bake at 190 °C for fifty minutes, sprinkle it with water and cover it with a cloth for ten minutes.

summary.en: Minced pork fried with chilli, garlic and holy basil. Five minutes from start to plate.

text.en: Pound the garlic and chillies to a rough paste in a mortar. A mortar gives a different result from a knife: the juices come out and reach the oil.
Mix the oyster, fish and soy sauces with the sugar in a cup — there will be no time once the pan is hot.
Heat the wok with two spoons of oil, throw in the paste and fry for twenty seconds, to the smell.
Add the pork and leave it alone for a minute, then break it up and fry two minutes more. Pour in the sauce and let it coat the meat.
Off the heat, stir in the basil — the residual heat wilts it in seconds. In the same pan fry the eggs in the rest of the oil until the edges go lacy.

summary.en: Gruyère and Vacherin melted in white wine with starch. The acidity of the wine keeps the cheese from seizing.

text.en: Rub the inside of the pot with a cut clove of garlic and leave it in.
Toss both grated cheeses with the cornflour by hand until every shred is coated.
Warm the wine with the lemon juice until bubbles appear at the edge, but not to a boil.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring in a figure of eight until each is fully melted before the next goes in.
When the mass turns even and strings from the spoon, add the kirsch and season with nutmeg and pepper.
Move it to the burner and keep the flame at its lowest. The bread is speared through the crust rather than the crumb.

summary.en: Meat on skewers in a tamarind and spice marinade, grilled over coals at the roadside.

text.en: Mix the tamarind, crushed garlic and ginger, all the spices, oil and salt into a marinade.
Cut the meat into one-and-a-half-centimetre cubes and coat it in the marinade.
Refrigerate for at least four hours, ideally overnight.
Thread the pieces onto skewers packed close, without gaps.
Get the coals hot — you should not be able to hold a palm above the grate for more than three seconds.
Grill a minute and a half on each of four sides, basting with the leftover marinade.
Slide the meat off the skewers into flatbread, add raw onion and serve at once.

summary.en: Veal beaten to three millimetres, crumbed and fried in plenty of fat until the coating puffs away.

text.en: Beat the meat between two sheets of film to three millimetres. Use the flat side of the mallet, not the toothed one: teeth tear the fibres.
Beat the eggs to an even liquid without foam. Salt the meat and coat it in flour, then egg, then crumbs.
Do not press the crumbs on. The coating has to sit loosely; only then will it lift and puff.
Heat a centimetre of fat to 170 °C and lower the schnitzel in. Fry two minutes, swirling the pan the whole time so fat washes over the top.
Turn it and give it ninety seconds more, to gold. Drain on a rack and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.

summary.en: Guanciale, tomato and pecorino. No onion, no garlic, no olive oil — the fat comes from the meat.

text.en: Put the guanciale into a cold dry pan and turn on a medium flame. A slow start renders the fat completely; a hot pan burns the outside and leaves it tough within.
When the pieces turn glassy and gold at the edges, lift half of them out for the top. Pour in the wine and let it cook away.
Crush the tomatoes by hand, add them with the chilli and simmer for ten minutes. The sauce should thicken without losing its red.
Boil the bucatini a minute short, move it into the sauce with a ladle of its water and finish it over the flame for half a minute.
Off the heat, stir in the pecorino and serve. The reserved guanciale goes on top with a little more cheese.

summary.en: Tomatoes and peppers stuffed with herbed rice and baked with potatoes in olive oil.

text.en: Cut lids off the tomatoes and scoop out the flesh with a spoon without piercing the walls.
Blitz the flesh and add the sugar; it takes the edge off the tomato acidity.
Soften the onion in olive oil for ten minutes, until sweet.
Mix the raw rice with the onion, herbs, half the tomato purée, salt and pepper.
Fill the vegetables two-thirds full, cap them with their lids and set them in a dish.
Tuck potato wedges between them, pour over the remaining purée and douse it all with oil.
Bake covered with foil at 180 °C for an hour, then uncover and give it twenty minutes more.

summary.en: Chopped chicken in a thin broth with ginger, garlic and chilli. Bhutanese everyday cooking.

text.en: Chop the chicken through the bone into pieces about the size of a matchbox.
Pound the ginger and garlic to a coarse paste.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the paste and cook it two minutes.
Add the chicken and fry five minutes, until it whitens all over.
Add the tomatoes and chillies, pour in water a finger above and season.
Simmer twenty minutes; the broth should stay thin.
Stir in the coriander and serve in deep bowls with red rice.

summary.en: Swabian egg noodles layered with cheese and buried under fried onion.

text.en: Mix the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg and beat the dough with a spoon for a good five minutes, until bubbles rise and it starts to string off the spoon.
While the dough rests, fry the onion in butter over medium heat until deep gold. That is twenty minutes, not five — the sugars need the time to caramelise.
Press the dough into boiling salted water through a spätzle grater or a wide-holed colander. They float within a minute; lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Layer them into a warm dish: spätzle, cheese, spätzle, cheese. The heat of the noodles melts it; no oven is needed.
Bury it under the fried onion and serve at once. The classic side is a green salad with a vinegar dressing, and it is a counterweight rather than a garnish.

summary.en: A long-fermented dough, uncooked tomato, mozzarella and basil. Time decides everything here, not the number of ingredients.

text.en: Dissolve the yeast in the water, add the flour and mix to a rough dough. Rest it twenty minutes, then work in the salt and knead ten minutes to a smooth ball.
Leave it two hours at room temperature, divide it into four balls and refrigerate for a day.
Take the dough out three hours before baking. Crush the tomatoes by hand with a pinch of salt: the sauce is done.
Heat the oven with a stone or steel at full power for at least an hour. It takes longer than seems necessary and it is not optional.
Stretch a ball with your fingers from the centre outwards, leaving the rim untouched. No rolling pin: it drives the air out of the rim and the crust will not rise.
Spread a thin layer of sauce, lay on the mozzarella and trickle over the oil. Bake seven to nine minutes, until the rim is spotted, and add the basil to the finished pizza.

photo.author: Dale Cruse from San Francisco, CA, USA

summary.en: Tomato, cucumber and pepper under a cap of grated white cheese. The vegetables are cut large, the cheese grated fine.

text.en: Char the peppers over a flame until the skin blackens, close them in a covered dish for ten minutes and peel them.
Cut the tomatoes and cucumbers into two-centimetre dice and the peppers into strips.
Mix the vegetables with the onion and parsley and dress with the oil, vinegar and salt.
Mound it on a dish and blanket it with the grated cheese without stirring. Finish with olives.

summary.en: Rice with prawns, ham and egg, where every grain stays separate under a thin film of egg.

text.en: Separate two yolks and rub them through the cold rice with your hands until every grain is coated. Beat the remaining eggs separately.
Heat the wok with a spoon of oil until it smokes, pour in the beaten eggs, let them set and break them into pieces. Set them aside.
Fry the prawns for ninety seconds, add the ham, carrot and peas and cook a minute more. Add them to the eggs.
Add the rest of the oil, tip in the rice and fry three minutes at full heat, tossing constantly. The grains should be jumping in the wok, not sitting in it.
Return everything to the wok, pour the wine down the side and add the soy, season and toss for thirty seconds more. Scatter over the spring onion.

summary.en: A potato purée soup with finely shredded kale and slices of smoked chouriço.

text.en: Soften the onion and garlic in half the olive oil for eight minutes.
Add the diced potato, cover with a litre and a half of water and boil twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Blend the soup to a smooth purée and season it.
Fry the chouriço slices in a dry pan until they colour and drain them on paper.
Roll the kale leaves tightly and cut across them into threads.
Bring the purée to the boil, add the kale and cook it exactly three minutes.
Ladle it out, add the sausage slices and pour over raw olive oil.

summary.en: A soup of matsun and wheat groats. The whole difficulty is keeping the yoghurt base from splitting.

text.en: Soak the dzavar overnight, then boil it in a litre of water until soft, about twenty-five minutes. Keep the water.
Whisk the matsun with the egg and flour until completely smooth. No lumps may remain; each one becomes a curd in the soup.
Pour the mixture into a cold pan and heat it over medium, stirring with a wooden spoon in one direction, until it comes to a boil.
At the first bubbles, stir in the wheat with its cooking water and hold it on a low heat for five more minutes.
Fry the onion in butter until golden and stir it into the soup with the dried mint. Salt to taste.
Ladle out and scatter with coriander. Spas must not be boiled twice; reheat it only until hot.

summary.en: Chicken braised in soy sauce with vinegar, garlic and bay. The vinegar is left unstirred for the first ten minutes.

text.en: Marinate the chicken in the soy with the crushed garlic and peppercorns for thirty minutes.
Lift the chicken out, dry it and brown it skin down. Keep the marinade.
Pour in the marinade, water and vinegar, add the bay and sugar. Bring it to the boil and neither stir nor cover for ten minutes.
Cover and simmer for twenty-five minutes, turning the chicken once.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for five to ten minutes, spooning it over the chicken. Serve with rice.

summary.en: Steamed fermented cassava couscous with grilled fish and a sharp onion salad.

text.en: Grind the garlic, ginger, chilli, stock cube, salt and oil into a paste.
Slash the fish at the sides and rub the paste inside the cuts and over the skin. Leave it twenty minutes.
Break up the attiéké with your hands, sprinkle it with hot water and salt it.
Cover it and let it steam ten minutes, in a steamer or simply covered somewhere warm.
Slice the onion, tomatoes and chilli and mix them with lemon juice, salt and a spoon of oil.
Grill the fish over coals or in a griddle pan, seven minutes a side.
Serve the attiéké, fish and salad on one plate, with a wedge of lemon.

summary.en: A whole fish on the grate with lemon myrtle and lime, part in foil and part over direct heat.

text.en: Cut three slashes on each side of the fish and pat it completely dry.
Work the garlic with the butter, lemon myrtle, lime zest, salt and pepper.
Rub the mixture into the slashes and the cavity and tuck slices of lime and fennel inside.
Wrap the fish in foil with the seams on top so the juices do not run out.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat under the fish has to be indirect.
Cook it in the foil for twenty minutes, turning the parcel once halfway.
Unwrap it, move the fish onto an oiled grate over the coals and give it a minute a side for the crust.

summary.en: Layers of fried pita, hot chickpeas and garlic yoghurt with browned butter and pine nuts.

text.en: Boil the chickpeas in unsalted water for ninety minutes, until completely soft, and keep the water.
Tear the pitas into two-finger pieces and fry them in oil to a golden crisp.
Whisk the yoghurt with the tahini, crushed garlic, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Let the yoghurt mixture down with a couple of spoons of the chickpea water to the body of thick cream.
Fry the pine nuts in the ghee until golden and take them off the heat.
Spread the fried bread in a dish and top it with the hot chickpeas and a spoon of their liquid.
Pour over the yoghurt, spoon on the butter and nuts, dust with paprika and parsley and serve at once.

summary.en: Cod in beer batter with twice-fried chips. The batter lives on cold and on the gas in the beer.

text.en: Rinse the cut potatoes of their starch, dry them thoroughly and fry at 140 °C for six minutes. They should turn soft but stay pale. Set them aside to cool.
Mix the flour, cornflour and baking powder. Pour in the ice-cold beer and whisk only a few strokes — lumps are fine, an over-mixed batter turns tough.
Dry the fish, dust it in plain flour and shake off the excess. Without that the batter slides off in the oil.
Heat the oil to 190 °C. Dip the fish, let the excess run off and lower it in, holding it for a couple of seconds so it does not stick to the bottom. Fry six minutes.
Lift the fish out and finish the chips in the same oil for three minutes, until gold. Salt them at once, while hot.

summary.en: A clear broth of fresh tuna, cooked in water with salt and almost nothing else.

text.en: Cut the tuna into large pieces and rinse them under cold water.
Cover with a litre and a half of cold water, salt it and bring it up.
Skim for the first five minutes; the clarity of the broth depends on it.
Add the curry leaves and pandan and cook twenty minutes on the lowest heat.
Remove the leaves, check the salt and take it off the heat.
Serve with rice, sliced onion, chilli and lime, each person adding them to their own bowl.

summary.en: Rice, lentils and pasta in one bowl under a vinegary tomato sauce and fried onion.

text.en: Fry the onion in the oil over medium heat for twenty-five minutes to a deep brown, stirring. Drain it on paper; it crisps as it cools.
Boil the lentils for twenty minutes to soft but not collapsing, and drain.
Cook the rice in the onion oil: fry it two minutes, add water at one and a half to one and cook covered for fifteen minutes.
Boil the pasta and drain it. For the sauce, fry the garlic in a spoon of oil to gold, pour in the vinegar and let it reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes, cumin and chilli and cook twenty minutes to a thick sauce. Season.
Build it in the bowl in layers: rice, lentils, pasta, chickpeas, sauce, fried onion. The mixing happens at the table.

summary.en: Yoghurt-marinated chicken, roasted, in a tomato and cream sauce finished with fenugreek.

text.en: Mix the yoghurt with half the ginger, garlic and spices, season it and marinate the chicken for at least an hour, better overnight.
Roast the chicken at 220 °C for twenty minutes, or sear it in a screaming-hot pan until it takes dark scorch marks. It can stay slightly underdone inside — the sauce will finish it.
Melt the butter and fry the onion with the rest of the ginger and garlic until golden. Add the tomatoes and the spices and cook for fifteen minutes.
Blend the sauce with the soaked cashews until completely smooth and return it to the pan. It is the cashews, not flour, that give the sauce its body.
Return the chicken to the sauce, pour in the cream and warm it through for five minutes without letting it boil. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms, stir it in and take the pan off.

summary.en: Flaked boiled fish mashed with potato in a white sauce. Icelandic home cooking made from leftovers.

text.en: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, peel them and cut them into large pieces.
Poach the cod in salted water for eight minutes, lift it out and flake it by hand, removing bones and skin.
Fry the onion in butter until soft, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes, stirring.
Pour in the milk in a thin stream, whisking continuously, and bring the sauce to the thickness of cream.
Stir in the mustard, salt and pepper, add the fish and potato and warm everything through for five minutes.
Mash with a fork to a coarse, uneven texture in which the pieces are still recognisable, and scatter with chives.

summary.en: A Provençal vegetable stew where each vegetable is cooked separately before they meet — otherwise it turns to mush.

text.en: Fry the aubergine over high heat in two spoons of oil until the edges brown, then set it aside. Aubergine drinks oil instantly — do not add more, it gives it back later.
In the same pan, fry the courgette until golden, about four minutes, and add it to the aubergine. It should stay firm.
Fry the pepper until soft with a few charred spots and set it aside as well.
In the remaining oil, sweat the onion until soft, add the garlic and thyme and give it half a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook them down over medium heat into a thick sauce, about twenty minutes. It should hold on a spoon rather than run off it.
Return the vegetables to the pan, season and warm them through together for ten minutes over low heat. Take it off, add the basil and let it stand — ratatouille is better warm than hot.

summary.en: Spiced mince moulded onto a skewer and grilled over coals.

text.en: Grate the onions finely and wring them dry in muslin, discarding the juice.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry pan until it smells nutty and let it cool.
Mix the mince with the onion, ginger garlic paste, papaya, spices, coriander and chillies.
Work the mixture ten minutes, until it turns tacky and pulls back at your hand.
Fold in the chickpea flour and chill the mixture for at least an hour.
With wet hands mould the mince onto flat skewers in an even two-centimetre layer.
Grill over hot coals four minutes a side, basting with oil. Serve with naan.

summary.en: A plate-sized breaded steak over rice and potatoes, topped with a fried egg and raw salsa.

text.en: Pound the meat under film to three or four millimetres. Work from the centre outwards or it tears.
Season and press into breadcrumbs with the flat of your hand. No egg wash is used here.
Dice the tomato, onion and beetroot small, mix with the parsley, salt and a spoon of oil.
Fry the boiled potato slices until golden and keep them warm.
Fry the steaks a minute and a half a side in hot oil; meat this thin cooks instantly.
Fry the eggs, leaving the yolks runny.
Build it: rice, potato, the steak across the whole plate, the egg, and the raw salsa over the top.

summary.en: A breaded cutlet under tomato sauce, ham and melted cheese.

text.en: Pound the meat to five millimetres and season it.
Beat the eggs with crushed garlic and chopped parsley; that garlic in the egg wash is the Uruguayan touch.
Dip the pieces in the egg, then press them firmly into the breadcrumbs.
Let the coating set for fifteen minutes in the fridge.
Fry in hot oil three minutes a side, to a golden crust, and drain on a rack.
Lay the milanesas on a tray, spoon on the tomato sauce, cover with ham and cheese and dust with oregano.
Grill for four minutes, until the cheese melts and colours.

summary.en: Rice noodles fried with tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar. The whole thing takes four minutes.

text.en: Soak the noodles in warm water for twenty minutes. They should bend but still feel firm when you bite one.
Dissolve the palm sugar in the tamarind and fish sauce, warming them together for a minute. Taste it: sour, salty and sweet should all land equally.
Get the wok hot, fry the tofu until crisp, add the garlic and shallot, then after half a minute the prawns. Cook until pink and push them to the side.
Break the eggs into the cleared space, let them set and break them up with the spatula. Add the drained noodles and pour in the sauce.
Fry, tossing constantly, for two minutes until the noodles drink the sauce and soften. Add the sprouts and chives, toss once and take it off.

summary.en: Risotto with cuttlefish and its own ink. The ink goes in at the end, or it turns bitter.

text.en: Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft, add the cuttlefish and cook five minutes; it releases water.
Add half the wine and the tomato paste and stew covered for twenty-five minutes, topping up with stock, until the cuttlefish softens.
Add the rice and toast it two minutes, until the grains turn translucent at the edges. Pour in the rest of the wine.
Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for eighteen minutes. Each addition goes in when the last has nearly been absorbed.
Five minutes before the end stir in the ink. The risotto turns black within seconds.
Off the heat, beat in a spoon of olive oil and the parsley, cover for two minutes and serve.

summary.en: A soup of dashi and miso that takes ten minutes. Miso must never boil: boiling takes out both the aroma and the point of it.

text.en: Cover the kombu with cold water and set it over low heat. Bring it to the edge of a boil over about ten minutes and lift the seaweed out before bubbles appear.
Bring the water to the boil, add the bonito flakes, take it off the heat at once and let it stand for two minutes until the flakes sink.
Strain the stock through a sieve without pressing the flakes — pressed flakes turn it bitter.
Soak the wakame in cold water for five minutes; it swells several times over.
Warm the dashi, add the tofu and the wakame and hold it at a low heat for a couple of minutes.
Whisk the miso smooth in a ladle of the hot stock, stir it back in and take the pan off the heat immediately. Scatter over the spring onion.

summary.en: Pasta from four ingredients: guanciale, eggs, pecorino and pepper. There is no cream in it and never was.

ingredients.note: cut into short strips; pancetta works

text.en: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and salt it properly — this is the only salt in the dish, since the cheese and the guanciale bring their own.
Put the guanciale into a cold pan and turn the heat to medium. The fat should render gradually and the pieces turn golden and crisp at the edges, about 6 to 8 minutes.
While the fat renders, beat the yolks, the whole egg, the grated pecorino and the pepper into a thick paste. Let it sit at room temperature so it does not seize when it meets hot pasta.
Cook the spaghetti a minute short of the packet time. Before draining, save a cup of the cooking water — the sauce will not come together without it.
Take the pan off the heat, add the pasta and toss it through the fat. Let the pan cool for twenty seconds — it should be warm, not hot.
Pour in the egg mixture and stir hard, adding pasta water a spoonful at a time until the sauce turns glossy and coats every strand. Serve immediately.

summary.en: Meatballs on a panade of bread and cream, in a cream sauce, with lingonberry and mashed potato.

text.en: Soak the bread in a hundred millilitres of the cream for ten minutes and mash it to a paste.
Fry the onion in butter until soft and cool it completely: warm onion starts cooking the meat.
Mix both minces with the panade, onion, egg, allspice and salt, and work it for five minutes until tacky.
Roll walnut-sized balls with wet hands and fry them in butter in batches, shaking the pan so they roll and colour evenly.
In the same pan whisk the flour into the remaining fat, pour in the stock and the rest of the cream, add the soy and cook five minutes to a sauce.
Return the meatballs to the sauce and warm them through for five minutes. Serve with mashed potato, lingonberry and pickled cucumber.

summary.en: Red lentils in a berbere sauce. A fasting dish eaten in Ethiopia on fast days all year round.

text.en: Cook the onion dry in a pot for thirty minutes over medium heat, stirring, until it becomes a dark paste.
Pour in the oil, add the garlic and ginger and cook three minutes.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste and fry five minutes: the mixture darkens and turns fragrant.
Add the lentils, pour in the water and simmer twenty-five minutes, stirring, until the lentils fall apart.
Season at the end, cook it down to a porridge-thick stew and serve with injera or flatbread.

summary.en: A soup of jute leaves, slippery in texture, with a garlic and coriander tempering.

text.en: Simmer the chicken with the onion, cardamom and bay for forty-five minutes and strain the broth.
Chop the molokhia leaves finely with a mezzaluna or blitz them to an even green mass.
Bring the broth to the boil, add the leaves and immediately drop the heat to its lowest.
Hold the soup just below a simmer for ten minutes, stirring; it thickens and turns slippery.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste and fry it in ghee with the coriander until deep gold.
Pour the tempering into the soup — it will hiss — and cover the pot immediately for a minute.
Serve with boiled rice, the chicken and lemon, each in its own dish.

summary.en: Mashed potato crushed together with curly kale, with smoked sausage and a well of gravy.

text.en: Boil the potatoes in salted water for twenty minutes. Seven minutes before the end pile the kale on top to steam.
Meanwhile warm the sausage in water for twenty minutes without letting it boil: boiling splits the skin and the fat leaves.
Render the bacon until crisp and set it aside, keeping the fat.
Drain, crush the potato and kale together with a masher, working in the hot milk, butter, bacon fat and mustard.
Fold in the crackling, divide between plates, make a well and fill it with gravy. Slice the sausage and lay it over.

summary.en: Crab in a thick tomato-chilli sauce bound with egg, mopped up with fried mantou buns.

text.en: Joint the crab: lift the shell, cut the body into four and crack the claws with the back of a knife.
Pound the garlic, ginger and chillies to a paste and fry it in oil for three minutes, until fragrant.
Add the sambal, ketchup, sugar and vinegar and cook two minutes, until the sauce darkens.
Pour in the stock, bring it up and add the crab pieces. Cover and cook eight minutes.
Slake the cornflour in cold water and stir it in to thicken the sauce.
Turn off the heat and pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream, stirring once in a circle.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the fried mantou.

summary.en: Maize porridge with potato, beaten with cheese and kajmak until it pulls into threads.

text.en: Boil the cut potatoes in salted water for twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Without draining, rain in the maize flour in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook on a low heat for fifteen minutes, stirring with a wooden paddle; the porridge catches quickly.
Mash the potato in the pot together with the porridge until uniform.
Work in the crumbled cheese and kajmak, adding hot milk, and beat with the paddle for five minutes.
Turn it into a bowl, make a hollow and pour in melted butter. Serve at once.

summary.en: Two layers of bulgur and meat with a filling of mince and pine nuts between them, baked in a tray.

text.en: Soak the bulgur in cold water for twenty minutes and squeeze it completely dry.
Blitz the lean beef with one onion to a paste and work in the bulgur, salt and half the spices.
Knead the mass five minutes, wetting your hands, until it is smooth and tacky.
Fry the remaining onion, add the minced lamb, the spices and the pine nuts and cook ten minutes.
Press half the mass into an oiled tray in a one-centimetre layer, smoothing it with a wet palm.
Spread the filling and cover with the other half of the mass, smoothed the same way.
Cut it into diamonds down to the base, pour over the olive oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, to a browned crust.

summary.en: Tanzanian fish curry on coconut milk with tamarind and curry powder.

text.en: Rub the fish steaks with salt and half the curry powder and leave them fifteen minutes.
Fry the fish two minutes a side to a crust and lift it onto a plate.
Soften the onion in the same pan and add the garlic and ginger.
Add the remaining curry powder and warm it a minute, until the aroma lifts.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and reduce them to a thick base without loose liquid.
Pour in the coconut milk with the tamarind and warm it without letting it boil.
Return the fish to the sauce, let it sit five minutes and serve with rice and coriander.

summary.en: Potato dressed in warm stock with vinegar and oil. No mayonnaise — southern Germany does not admit it here.

text.en: Boil the potatoes in their skins until done, about twenty minutes from the boil. Test with a knife: it should go in without dropping through.
While they cook, warm the stock with the onion, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper, without letting it boil.
Peel the potatoes while hot, holding them on a fork, and slice them three or four millimetres thick straight into the bowl.
Pour the hot dressing over and leave it twenty minutes, turning it once. The potato drinks almost all of the liquid.
Add the oil, turn it again and taste. It should be slightly sharper than feels right; the flavour settles as it stands.

summary.en: Lamb in a thick gravy under mashed potato, baked to a browned crust.

text.en: Fry the mince over a high flame, leaving it alone for the first minute so it takes dark colour. Lift it out, pouring off the excess fat.
In the same pan fry the onion and carrot for eight minutes, add the flour and tomato paste and cook two minutes.
Return the meat, pour in the stock and Worcestershire, add the thyme and cook uncovered for twenty minutes, until the gravy is thick.
Boil the potatoes and mash them with the butter and hot milk until smooth, seasoning generously. The mash should be firm rather than pourable.
Stir the peas into the meat, put it in a dish, cover with the mash and score the top with a fork.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes until browned. Let it stand ten minutes before cutting.

summary.en: Hilsa in a ground mustard sauce, cooked by steaming. The great fish of Bengal.

ingredients.note: yellow and black in equal parts

text.en: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for twenty minutes.
Grind them with two chillies, a pinch of salt and a little water into a smooth paste.
Rub the fish steaks with turmeric and salt and leave them ten minutes.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off and let it cool a minute; raw mustard oil is acrid.
Add the nigella, pour in the mustard paste let down with half a cup of water, and cook three minutes.
Lay the fish in a single layer, add the remaining chillies whole, cover and stew twelve minutes.
Finish with a spoon of raw mustard oil, take it off the heat and serve with rice.

summary.en: Pork in a marinade of dried chillies and pineapple, seared to caramelised edges, in a corn tortilla.

ingredients.note: or a teaspoon of ground annatto

text.en: Seed the chillies and toast them in a dry pan until they smell — twenty seconds a side, no longer, or they turn bitter. Cover with boiling water for fifteen minutes.
Blend the softened chillies with half the pineapple, the achiote, vinegar, garlic, cumin and oregano to a smooth paste. Season it.
Coat the pork in the marinade and leave it at least two hours, ideally overnight. Do not go past a day: the pineapple will soften the meat to mush.
Get a pan searing hot and cook the meat in batches, two minutes a side. Do not stir until dark edges appear.
Sear the rest of the pineapple in the same pan and dice it. Chop the meat roughly, warm the tortillas twenty seconds a side and build: meat, pineapple, onion, coriander, lime.

summary.en: Veal strips in a creamy mushroom sauce with white wine, served with rösti.

text.en: Cut the veal into fine strips across the grain and pat them dry.
Heat a pan with butter and sear the meat in batches for thirty seconds, moving it onto a plate.
Fry the shallot and mushrooms in the same pan until their water has gone.
Stir in the flour, cook it a minute and add the wine, reducing it by half.
Add the stock and cream and reduce the sauce to a coating consistency, about eight minutes.
Return the meat with its collected juices, warm it a minute without boiling, and add lemon.
Scatter with parsley and serve with rösti set alongside rather than under the meat.

summary.en: Purses of stiff dough holding chopped meat and broth. The broth appears on its own, from water worked into the filling.

text.en: Knead a dough from the flour, water and a pinch of salt. It should come out noticeably stiffer than a dumpling dough — hard work to knead. Wrap it and rest it for forty minutes.
Chop the meat by hand into pieces a few millimetres across. Mix it with the onion, coriander, cumin, salt and pepper.
Work the iced water into the filling a little at a time until the mixture turns sticky and stops taking any more. Chill it for twenty minutes.

Roll out discs 12 cm across and about two millimetres thick. Put a tablespoon of filling in the middle and gather the edge in pleats all the way round — eighteen at the least. Twist the top and pinch it shut.
Drop them into a large pot of salted boiling water, swirling the water with a slotted spoon first so they do not stick. Boil for seven or eight minutes after they float.

summary.en: A thick pork and sausage gravy on soured cream, into which pancakes are dipped. Hence the name.

text.en: Brown the pork well, add the onion and fry until soft.
Add the sliced sausage and ribs, pour in a cup of water, add the bay and stew twenty-five minutes.
Whisk the flour into the soured cream until smooth and stir it into the pot.
Simmer ten minutes on a low heat, until the gravy thickens to the consistency of pouring cream.
Whisk a pancake batter from the flour, milk, eggs and salt and let it stand fifteen minutes.
Cook thin unsweetened pancakes in a dry pan.
Serve the machanka in a deep bowl with the pancakes stacked beside it. You tear off a piece and dip.

summary.en: Fried chicken with fried plantain and vegetables. The dish called "the director general's chicken".

text.en: Marinate the chicken in crushed garlic, ginger, thyme, salt and pepper for half an hour.
Fry the chicken in oil until browned all over and lift it out.
Cut the plantain into large pieces and fry it in the same oil, to caramelised edges.
Pour off most of the oil and fry the onion, tomatoes and pepper until soft.
Return the chicken, add the carrot, beans and the whole scotch bonnet, pour in a cup of water and stew twenty minutes.
Remove the chilli, fold in the plantain and warm it three minutes. Serve at once.

summary.en: Shredded chicken in a creamy sauce of ají amarillo, nuts and bread.

text.en: Poach the chicken breast in salted water for twenty minutes and pull it into fine threads by hand.
Soak the crustless bread in the milk for ten minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add the ají paste and turmeric and cook five minutes.
Blend the soaked bread with its milk, the walnuts and the fried onion until smooth.
Return the mixture to the pan and cook it ten minutes on a low heat, stirring.
Stir in the chicken and parmesan, season and warm it five minutes to the thickness of soured cream.
Serve over boiled potato and rice, garnished with egg and olives.

summary.en: Chicken with onion and sumac on taboon bread soaked in olive oil.

text.en: Rub the chicken with salt, pepper, allspice, cardamom and cinnamon and leave it half an hour.
Slice the onions into thin half-moons; a kilo and a half takes about twenty minutes.
Stew the onions in the olive oil over a low heat for forty minutes, until translucent and sweet.
Stir two-thirds of the sumac and salt into the onions and give them five more minutes.
Brown the chicken and roast it at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden, watching that they do not scorch.
Lay down the bread, the onions on it, the chicken on top, spoon over the pan oil and scatter with sumac and nuts.

summary.en: Rice in a wide pan with chicken, rabbit and beans. It is never stirred once, and the crust on the bottom depends on that.

name.en: Bomba rice, or another short grain

text.en: Heat the oil in a wide pan and brown the chicken and rabbit on every side. This is not a five-minute job: it takes a good quarter of an hour, and there is no point rushing it — the flavour of the whole dish is laid down here.
Push the meat to the edges, put the green beans in the middle and fry them for a couple of minutes. Add the grated tomato and the paprika and cook until the tomato darkens and stops smelling raw.
Pour in the stock, add the rosemary, saffron and white beans, salt it noticeably harder than feels right and let it boil for ten minutes. This is the last moment you can correct the seasoning.
Scatter the rice in an even layer and level it once with a spoon. After that do not touch the pan again — no stirring, no smoothing.
Cook on a high flame for ten minutes, then drop to medium for another eight, until the stock is gone. The rice should be showing above the surface.
Turn the heat up for half a minute and listen: the moment the sound turns from bubbling to a dry crackle, take it off. That is the socarrat. Cover with a cloth and let it stand for five minutes.

summary.en: Dumplings of potato and curd cheese, served with fried onion and soured cream.

text.en: Pour the boiling water with the oil and salt over the flour, work it with a spoon and then, once it cools, by hand for eight minutes. Cover and rest it half an hour.
Fry two of the onions in butter to a deep gold. Half goes into the filling and half is kept for serving.
Mash the warm potato with the curd and the fried onion, and season generously. The filling has to be firm enough to hold its shape.
Roll the dough to two millimetres, cut discs with a glass, add a teaspoon of filling and pinch the edges dry — wet dough will not seal.
Boil in batches in a wide pot of salted water. Lift them out a minute after they float.
Serve with the rest of the fried onion and soured cream. Plenty of people fry the boiled pierogi in butter afterwards, which is equally correct.

summary.en: Pita with fried aubergine, boiled egg, amba and salad. The Iraqi-Israeli street classic.

text.en: Cook the eggs at the barest simmer for an hour, then cool them in cold water and peel them.
Slice the aubergines a centimetre thick, salt them and press them under a weight for half an hour.
Pat the slices dry and fry them in oil to a deep gold on both sides.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice, water and salt to the thickness of pouring cream.
Dice the tomatoes and cucumbers small and mix them with the parsley, lemon and salt.
Warm the pitas, cut them into pockets and spread tahini inside.
Layer in the aubergine, sliced egg and salad, and spoon over the amba, tahini and zhug.

summary.en: Fish in a coconut curry soured with goraka and built on roasted curry powder.

text.en: Soak the goraka in a cup of warm water for twenty minutes and keep the water.
Rub the fish with salt, turmeric and half the curry powder and leave it fifteen minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger, curry leaves, pandan, cinnamon and fenugreek until fragrant.
Add the remaining curry powder and chilli and warm them a minute without letting them scorch.
Add the thinned coconut milk with the goraka water and bring it to the boil.
Lay the fish steaks in a single layer, add the goraka and cook twelve minutes, rocking the pan.
Add the thick coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling. Serve with red rice.

summary.en: Slices of pork belly fried crisp, with potatoes and a parsley sauce.

text.en: Pat the belly slices dry with paper and salt them on both sides.
Lay them in a single layer in a cold dry pan and turn the heat to medium.
Fry eight minutes a side, pouring the rendered fat off into a cup as it collects.
Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender and peel them hot.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes without letting it colour.
Pour in the milk in a thin stream, whisking until smooth, and cook the sauce five minutes.
Stir in the mountain of chopped parsley, the nutmeg, salt and pepper and serve with the pork, potatoes and beetroot.
