summary.en: A soup of freekeh, the smoked green wheat, with lamb and mint. The first thing on the table in Ramadan.

text.en: Brown the meat with the onion and celery in ghee for ten minutes.
Add the grated tomato, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook five minutes.
Pour in two litres of boiling water, add the chickpeas and simmer forty minutes.
Rinse the freekeh, add it and cook twenty minutes more, stirring; the grain settles and catches.
Stir in the coriander five minutes before the end and loosen with water if the soup has gone too thick.
Ladle out, crumble dried mint over each bowl and add lemon juice.

summary.en: A tuna soup with cassava and pickled onion. Ecuadorians eat it for breakfast and treat it as a hangover cure.

text.en: Cure the onion in the juice of two limes with salt and leave it at least fifteen minutes.
Fry the garlic and tomatoes with the cumin for five minutes, add a litre and a half of water and bring it up.
Lower in the tuna whole and poach it fifteen minutes on a low heat. Fish does not tolerate a hard boil.
Lift out the fish, strain the broth and return it to the heat. Cook the cassava in it for twenty minutes, until soft.
Flake the tuna coarsely, discarding the dark parts, and return it to the pot for two minutes.
Ladle it out and top with the cured onion and its juice and coriander. Serve with a wedge of lime.

photo.author: Ministerio de Turismo Ecuador from Ecuador

summary.en: Soup from onions, stock and cheese-topped bread. All of the flavour comes from caramelisation, which takes forty minutes rather than twenty.

text.en: Melt the butter in a heavy pot, add the onions and a pinch of salt, and keep them over medium heat, stirring every few minutes. For the first twenty minutes the onions give up water.
Then the caramelisation proper begins: another twenty-five minutes to take the onions to the colour of strong tea. If they catch, lower the heat and add a spoonful of water.
Stir in the flour and cook it out for a couple of minutes so it loses its raw taste.
Pour in the wine and scrape everything stuck to the bottom back into the pot. Let it reduce by half.
Add the stock and thyme, bring to the boil and simmer for twenty minutes. Season at the end, since the stock may already be salty.
Ladle into ovenproof bowls, top each with a slice of baguette, cover with cheese and put them under the grill until bubbling and browned, about three minutes.

summary.en: A sour soup of fermented dried greens with potato, soybeans and chilli.

text.en: Soak the gundruk in warm water for ten minutes and squeeze it out, keeping the water.
Toast the soybeans in a dry pan until they darken in patches and crack.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off and let it cool a minute; raw mustard oil is acrid.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and turmeric, add the tomatoes and cook five minutes.
Add the gundruk, soybeans and potato, and pour in the soaking water and a litre of water.
Cook twenty-five minutes, until the potato and beans are soft, and season.
Sizzle the dried chillies, fenugreek and timur in a spoon of oil and pour it into the soup.

summary.en: Pork with mushrooms and peppers, stewed in a clay pot under an egg.

text.en: Brown the diced pork in oil on all sides.
Add the onion and peppers and fry seven minutes, until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook over a high flame until their water has gone.
Take it off the heat, stir in the paprika and savory, add the wine and return it to the heat for three minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season, and divide everything between the pots.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, covered.
Take the lids off, break an egg into each pot, scatter the cheese and give them eight minutes more.

summary.en: Hand-chopped raw beef worked with spiced niter kibbeh butter and mitmita spice.

text.en: Melt the butter over a low heat with the ginger, garlic, cardamom, cinnamon and fenugreek.
Hold it twenty minutes without boiling, until the foam settles and the butter turns clear.
Strain the niter kibbeh through muslin and keep it warm.
Trim every membrane and sinew from the beef and chop it very fine with a knife, almost to a paste.
Work the warm niter kibbeh, mitmita and salt into the meat by hand for two minutes.
Warm the mixture in a pan for thirty seconds to body temperature, without letting it whiten.
Serve it on injera with the ayib cheese and stewed greens alongside.

summary.en: A creamy mushroom soup with dill, potato and a poached egg, sharpened with vinegar.

text.en: Boil the diced potato in a litre and a half of water with the caraway and bay for fifteen minutes.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in butter until their water has gone and add them to the pot.
Cook them together ten minutes so the mushrooms give their flavour to the broth.
Whisk the soured cream with the flour until smooth and lump-free.
Take the soup off the heat, stir in the cream mixture, return it to a low flame and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Add the vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper and most of the dill and taste for the balance of sour against creamy.
Poach the eggs in acidulated water and set one into each bowl, scattered with the remaining dill.

summary.en: Finnish salmon soup with potato and cream, a heap of dill and a knob of butter in the bowl.

text.en: Cover the head and bones with a litre and a half of water, add the allspice and bay, and simmer twenty-five minutes, skimming. Strain it.
Fry the leek and carrot in butter for five minutes without letting them colour.
Pour in the strained stock, add the potato and cook fifteen minutes until soft.
Add the cream and warm it without boiling. Season.
Slip in the pieces of salmon and hold them at a bare simmer for exactly five minutes. The fish should stay in whole pieces.
Ladle into bowls and add a knob of butter and a generous handful of dill to each.

summary.en: A pork chop with a pocket stuffed with Njeguši prosciutto and cheese, fried in breadcrumbs.

text.en: Cut each piece along its length, stopping short of the far edge, and open it like a book.
Beat the opened meat lightly under film and season the inside.
Lay in a slice of prosciutto and a slab of cheese, close it and press the edges together.
Coat in flour, egg and crumbs, then repeat the egg and crumbs a second time.
Chill for twenty minutes; the coating sets and will not slide off in the pan.
Fry over medium heat, six minutes a side, to a deep gold.
Drain on a rack, rest it five minutes and serve with fried potatoes and lemon.

summary.en: A cold beetroot soup on kefir, vivid pink, with cucumber, dill and boiled potatoes served alongside.

text.en: Boil the beetroot until tender, cool it completely and grate it coarsely.
Cut the cucumbers into matchsticks and chop the dill and spring onion.
Mix the beetroot, cucumber and herbs with the soured cream and salt it now, before the kefir, so the salt disperses.
Pour in the cold kefir and stir. The soup turns an even pink.
Chill it for an hour. Warm šaltibarščiai makes no sense.
Boil the potatoes and serve them hot on a separate plate. Put halved eggs into the soup.

summary.en: Chicken skewers over coals with a thick peanut sauce and sweet kecap manis.

text.en: Cut the chicken into two-centimetre cubes and coat them in a mix of kecap manis, garlic, coriander and turmeric.
Marinate for at least two hours, ideally overnight in the fridge.
Grind the peanuts to a coarse crumb, keeping a few whole for serving.
Fry the shallot, garlic and chilli in oil until soft, add the ground peanuts and cook three minutes.
Add a cup of water, the tamarind, palm sugar and kecap manis and cook the sauce ten minutes to thicken.
Thread the pieces tight onto soaked skewers, five or six to each.
Grill over hot coals two minutes a side, basting with kecap manis. Serve with the sauce and rice.

summary.en: Pork stewed with mushrooms, onion and wine in an individual clay pot, under cheese.

text.en: Brown the diced pork in oil on all sides.
Add the onion and pepper and fry until soft, seven minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook over a high heat for five minutes, until their water has gone.
Take it off the heat, stir in the paprika, garlic and tomato paste, add the wine and return it to the heat for three minutes.
Divide between clay pots, top up with water to the level of the meat, season and cover.
Bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes.
Take the lids off, cover with grated kashkaval and give it ten more minutes, to a browned cheese crust.

summary.en: Vegetables and prawns in an ice-cold lumpy batter. Whisking it smooth is exactly what must not happen.

text.en: Score the prawns three times on the inner curve and straighten them slightly, so they do not curl into rings in the oil.
Combine the dashi, soy and mirin, bring them to the boil and take them off: this is tentsuyu. Serve it with grated daikon.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Only when it is ready do you mix the batter — not before.
Beat the cold egg into the iced water, tip in the flour and cornflour and stir with chopsticks for five or six strokes. Leave the lumps.
Dust the pieces in dry flour, dip them in the batter and lower them in three or four at a time. Fry ninety seconds to two minutes.
Drain on a rack, never on paper. Between batches skim the floating scraps of batter out of the oil: they burn and taint the flavour.

summary.en: Rice and lentils fried before the water goes in. Bengali food for a rainy day.

text.en: Dry-roast the moong dal for five minutes, to a nutty smell, and rinse it.
Rinse the rice and dry it. Wet rice will not toast; it steams in its own water.
Heat the ghee, brown the potatoes and lift them out.
In the same ghee fry the bay, cinnamon and cardamom, then the onion and ginger until golden.
Add the rice and dal with the turmeric and cumin and toast them five minutes, stirring.
Add boiling water at twice the volume of the grain, return the potatoes, season and add the whole chillies.
Cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat, then let it stand ten minutes without opening it.

summary.en: Rice under separately cooked vegetables, meat and an egg, mixed with gochujang right before eating.

text.en: Marinate the beef in soy, garlic and a spoon of sesame oil for twenty minutes.
Blanch the spinach for thirty seconds, squeeze it dry and dress with sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Boil the sprouts three minutes and dress them the same way, with garlic.
Fry the carrot and the mushrooms separately, a couple of minutes each, seasoning each on its own. No need to wash the pan in between.
Sear the beef over a high flame for two minutes. Fry the eggs separately, leaving the yolks runny.
Divide the hot rice between bowls, arrange the vegetables and beef in sections, and top with an egg and a spoon of gochujang. Each person does the mixing.

summary.en: A bake of spiced mince with dried fruit under an egg and milk custard. South Africa's national dish.

text.en: Soak the bread in half the milk for ten minutes and squeeze it out, keeping the milk.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the curry powder and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the mince and cook, breaking up lumps, until it loses its pink, about ten minutes.
Stir in the bread, apricots, raisins, chutney, vinegar, salt and pepper and take it off the heat.
Press it into a dish, level it and bake at 180 °C for forty minutes.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk, pour it over, stand the bay leaves in the custard and scatter the almonds.
Return it to the oven for twenty minutes, until the custard sets and turns golden.

summary.en: A lunch plate of rice, beans, salad, plantain and meat, each in its own sector.

text.en: Marinate the chicken in lime juice, garlic, Salsa Lizano, salt and pepper for twenty minutes.
Cook the rice loose and warm the beans with a spoon of their liquid.
Dice the chayote and carrot small and stew them with garlic for ten minutes; that is the picadillo.
Fry the chicken over medium heat, six minutes a side.
Fry the ripe plantain slices to a caramel colour.
Toss the shredded cabbage with tomato, coriander, lime juice and salt.
Build the plate in sectors: rice, beans, chicken, picadillo, salad, plantain — unmixed.

summary.en: A thick clam soup with cream, potato and bacon. No tomato — that is a matter of principle.

text.en: Scrub the clams and steam them in a cup of water, covered, for five minutes, until they open. Discard any that stay shut. Strain the liquor through muslin: sand settles in it.
Take the meat from the shells and chop it coarsely. Set it aside; it returns at the very end.
Render the bacon in the pot, add the butter, onion and celery, and sweat them for eight minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour, cook it two minutes, pour in the strained clam liquor and the milk, and add the potato, thyme and bay.
Simmer for fifteen minutes until the potato is soft. Crush a few pieces against the side: the soup thickens without more flour.
Pour in the cream, return the clams and warm through for two minutes without boiling. Check the salt and serve with crackers.

summary.en: Lentil soup with rice and a vegetable tarkari. Nepal's everyday meal, eaten twice a day for a lifetime.

text.en: Rinse the lentils and boil them in a litre of water with the turmeric for thirty minutes, until they collapse completely. Skim for the first five minutes.
Start the rice. While it cooks, fry the onion, add the potato and cauliflower with a little turmeric and water, and cook fifteen minutes: that is the tarkari.
Fry the greens with garlic over a high flame for two minutes; they should stay bright.
For the jhaneko, heat the ghee and throw in the ajwain, cumin, dried chilli and garlic, frying twenty seconds to the smell.
Pour the sizzling spiced fat straight into the dal — it hisses. Stir, season and serve at once.
Build the plate: rice in the middle, dal in a small bowl, tarkari and greens around it, achar at the edge.

summary.en: Chicken spatchcocked and grilled over coals under a sauce of piri-piri, garlic and lemon.

text.en: Cut the chicken along the backbone, open it out and press it flat.
Blend the chillies, garlic, the juice of two lemons, paprika, vinegar, oregano, oil and salt.
Pour half the sauce into a separate bowl; that half is for basting.
Coat the chicken with the rest, working it under the skin, and refrigerate overnight.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat has to be indirect.
Grill the chicken skin up for thirty minutes, then turn it and give it fifteen more.
For the last five minutes baste with the reserved sauce mixed with melted butter. Serve with lemon.

summary.en: A whole pumpkin baked with rice, dried fruit and nuts. A festive dish, cut open at the table.

text.en: Cut the top off the pumpkin with its stalk; that is the lid. Scoop out the seeds and loose flesh with a spoon, leaving a wall two fingers thick.
Boil the rice in salted water for seven minutes, to half done, and drain.
Cover the dried fruit with boiling water for ten minutes, drain, and chop the apricots and prunes coarsely. Chop the nuts.
Mix the rice with the fruit, nuts, melted butter, honey and cinnamon. Salt it: a sweet filling without salt tastes flat.
Fill the pumpkin, without packing it down, put the cut lid back on and set it on a baking tray.
Bake at 180 °C for an hour and a half. Test at the side with a knife: it should go into the wall without resistance.
Rest fifteen minutes, carry it out whole and cut it into wedges from the crown to the base.

summary.en: Spiced fish wrapped in a banana leaf and baked in embers.

text.en: Slash the fish at the sides and rub it with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Grind the garlic, ginger and chilli to a paste and work it into the cuts and the cavity.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame so they turn pliable and stop cracking.
Lay tomato and onion slices on a leaf, the fish on them, then more tomato and spring onion.
Wrap in three leaves into a tight parcel and tie it with a strip of the same leaf.
Set the parcels on the coals and bake them fifteen minutes a side.
Serve them still in the leaf, with boiled cassava or rice.

summary.en: Green bananas stewed with beef in coconut milk. A Chagga dish from the slopes of Kilimanjaro.

text.en: Brown the beef, add the onion, garlic and ginger and fry until soft.
Add the tomatoes and curry powder and cook five minutes, until the tomatoes break down.
Add water level with the meat, season and stew thirty minutes, covered.
Peel the bananas under running water and cut them into thick rounds.
Add the bananas to the pot and cook twenty minutes, until tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm five minutes without letting it boil. Scatter with coriander.

summary.en: Kashmiri lamb in a yoghurt sauce with Kashmiri chilli, red from the chilli rather than from heat.

text.en: Warm the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves in the ghee until fragrant, one minute.
Add the asafoetida and the meat straight after, and brown it for ten minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Kashmiri chilli; over a flame it burns in seconds and turns bitter.
Return it to a low heat and add the whisked yoghurt a ladle at a time, stirring between each.
Add the fennel and dry ginger, season, and pour in a cup of hot water.
Braise covered for an hour and twenty on a low heat, until the meat comes away from the bone.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until oil rises to the surface. Serve with rice.

summary.en: Lamb baked under a thick yoghurt custard with egg and rice. Albania's national dish.

text.en: Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes, dotted with butter.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour and cook two minutes to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt, add the flour mixture and beat until completely smooth.
Stir in the rice. It takes up some of the moisture and keeps the custard from splitting.
Arrange the meat and its juices in a dish and pour the yoghurt mixture over.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, until the top colours and the centre still trembles slightly.
